intentionalDifferences: Go Server/router/broker mutexes, one connection forward goroutine and WebSocket write mutex become one owned Core actor, typed embedded Connection and optional network adapter. Actor operations preserve per-caller provider order and correlate replies independently. Reliable-queue saturation closes the slow peer rather than waiting on its socket; other peers continue. Local handlers also receive bounded deadlines and owned shutdown, unlike the unbounded Go local callback goroutine.

Go tokenless loopback listener is intentionally retired: every Rust network listener requires a host credential; embedded owner/service connections remain socket-free. Direct unconfigured HTTP helper predicates retain their compatibility truth value but are not a way to start an anonymous listener.

Go separately injected local/plain and local/identity maps become one startup Options.handler map whose later insertion replaces the earlier one. Live method inventory is a sorted unique union, and shadowed network registrations are withheld. Public runtime mutation of handler maps is not retained; production Go registration happens before Handler starts.

Rust credential identity is immutable per connection: plugin replacement/revocation serializes with admission and closes live peers; scoped tokens are reread every5seconds for scope/facade/provides changes. Legacy profile/yolo metadata remains inert and does not trigger revocation. Provider provides never becomes a caller method grant.

Rust adds explicit finite connection/pending/subscription/demand limits (1024/4096/512/4096) beyond the retained per-frame256 topic cap. Subscription acknowledgements report the actual retained set. Go per-caller forwarding queue256 is replaced by bounded actor/reliable channels; unbounded aggregate capacity is not a compatibility promise.

Host/Origin syntax fails closed more strictly in Rust: malformed nonempty Authorization is authoritative instead of falling through to query credentials; only valid HTTP(S) browser origins are accepted, malformed proxy configuration is rejected instead of silently ignored. Explicit proxy names, authority spelling, socket-local address and loopback/shared-bind behavior remain tested.

Only the Rust internal federation adapter stamps event.hub; wire publishers cannot assert peer provenance. Dispatch updates additionally require the currently registered negotiated execution provider; Go allowed host/spawn-granted publishers without that ownership proof. Negotiated ProviderCaller/cancel/callerClosed metadata is opt-in, preserving legacy ordinary frames while adding owned execution receipts.

Remote worker launch now requires explicit Peer.dispatch=true, including ownerless forwarded agents.spawn. Go used dispatch only to enable return-channel stamping and permitted an unowned fire-and-forget spawn without it. Linked visibility and ordinary qualified reads remain independent of dispatch. This is the stronger owned execution opt-in boundary; tests must opt in before claiming to exercise destination routing.
